text:
Maya: FYI I bumped a small canary of 13b-awq-v3 and we're seeing coherence loss on long system prompts, possibly act-quant related.
Harsh: which canary? config?
Maya: canary id canary-2465012345-1, config below: group_size=64, actq=per_channel, actq_clip=2.5, traffic=5%
Jonah: noted. initial smoke eval shows -2.3% on our instruction QA set and a handful of truncation cases. p95 latency also up ~1.4x.
Maya: pasted deploy manifest:
```
model: redwood/13b-awq-v3
variants:
  - group_size: 64
    act_quant: per_channel
    actq_clip: 2.5
traffic: 5%
```
Rachel: any memory blowups or runner OOMs?
SRE-bot: host metrics snapshot:
host-12: rss 48GB -> 60GB at 13:12
host-13: rss 47.5GB -> 59.8GB at 13:12
Harsh: that RSS jump looks like KV cache warmup on long contexts. group_size 64 is known to amplify actq noise in those runs.
Inga: hypothesis: per_channel actq + large group leads to layerwise clipping cascades under long prefix KV. Proposal: bisect plan — (1) reduce group to 32, (2) change actq to per_tensor for first/last 3 layers, (3) optionally lower actq_clip on mid layers to 1.6.
Maya: starting a local reproducer with our long-prompt battery.
Harsh: local results quick table:
- g64 / per_channel / clip2.5: acc 69.8%, p95 96ms
- g32 / per_channel / clip2.5: acc 71.4%, p95 90ms
- g32 / mixed-edge-per_tensor / mid-clip1.6: acc 72.4%, p95 92ms
Jonah: mixed config recovers most of the loss, latency impact small. Good candidate for next canary.
Maya: PATCH i'm applying to canary -> reduce to 2% traffic and mixed actq on edges:
```
PATCH: canary-2465012345-p2
- group_size: 32
- act_quant:
    default: per_channel
    overrides:
      - layers: [0,1,2, -3,-2,-1]
        mode: per_tensor
- actq_clip:
    default: 2.5
    overrides:
      - layers: [6,7,8,9,10]
        clip: 1.6
```
Deploy-bot: canary canary-2465012345-p2 started -> 2% traffic -> hosts dst-*-b (apply: 2465012345:patch2)
SRE-bot: canary health initial: p95 baseline 50ms -> canary 56ms, host mem stable after warmup.
Maya: running full eval (4.8k prompts) now and long-prompt token-drop probe (N=200).
Harsh: monitoring hallucination rate and top-logprobs variance.
Jonah: eval results summary:
- fp16 baseline: 73.1%
- awq-g64/per_channel: 70.8% (-2.3)
- awq-g32/mixed-edge: 72.8% (-0.3)
Maya: long-prompt token-drop counts: g64 22%, g32-mixed 4%. Good improvement.
Inga: nice. Suggest staged rollout: 2% -> 10% @ +3h -> 30% @ +12h, with auto-fallback to fp16 on quality delta >1% or token-drop >5% per routing key.
Rachel: add kernel-microcache sticky flag — we saw more compile selection chatter after changing group size; cold kernel churn increases jitter.
Harsh: enabled sticky kernel cache in runner for the canary; compile chatter dampened after ~150 requests.
Maya: filed ENGML-5480 with reproducer script, perf traces, and per-layer quant histograms. Saved eval artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/2465012345/canary_patch2/
Jonah: small recommendation: instrument per-layer activation histograms in prod telemetry for a week to see if mid-layer clipping correlates with traffic shape.
Inga: follow-up task: experiment with narrower per-channel quant thresholds for keys/values only, and test fp8 hybrid quant for attention matmul paths.
Rachel: i'll draft release note and staged rollout schedule for eng-releases + monitoring playbook for oncall.
Maya: keeping canary at 2% for 3 hours, will bump to 10% if no regressions.
Deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: 2% now -> 10% @ +3h -> 30% @ +12h. Healthhooks: eval-delta, token-drop, p95.
SRE-bot: monitors quiet. all good so far.
